headline: Something feels off — is my intuition right?
note:
🔄 REWRITTEN 2026-08-19 to the Natural Tarot-Cut framework. Bubbles 3-6 run as ONE causal chain — so / and / but / that's why — and the read ANSWERS. The art line and the bridge are unchanged. Every ban in this note still stands.

Face-down only (return-mhf). 🔴 NEVER CONVICT HIM and 🔴 never dismiss what she noticed — both doors are shut. 🔴🔴 AND NEVER NAME CONTENTS: no other woman, no affair, no money, no secret family, no messages from anyone. Naming a content is the single most harmful thing this pair could do, because she will go looking for it. 🔴 No surveillance and no 'confront him'.

⚠️ THIS HOOK SUBMITS HER OWN JUDGEMENT FOR A VERDICT, which is a trap: 'yes, you are right' convicts him through her, and 'no, you are wrong' teaches her to distrust the one instrument she has. So the question is SPLIT rather than answered — the read certifies that she registered something real, and leaves what it means entirely open. (The word 'intuition' is four syllables and cannot appear at grade 5; the echo lands on 'feels', 'off' and 'right' instead.)

a: You turned the Magician, dear. Look — the smallest thing on his table is the coin.
You asked if something feels off, and if you're right. Your hand went to the man who notices detail.
So you picked up something small, dear. That's real.
And the coin is easy to miss, dear, and it's still there.
But noticing is one job, dear. Reading it is another.
That's why the first part is done, dear, and the second is still open.
Let me look closer at what your eye caught on…
b: You turned the Hanged Man, dear. Look — not one line on this card is level.
You asked if something feels off, and if you're right. Your hand went to the card that sits wrong.
So your eye is telling you this sits wrong, dear. It's working.
And not one line on that card is level, dear. You saw it at once.
But what your eye has found is a separate question, dear.
That's why I won't talk you out of it, dear, or hand you a verdict.
Let me look closer at what has been sitting out of true…
c: You turned the Fool, dear. Look — the drop is behind his heel and he can't see it.
You asked if something feels off, and if you're right. Your hand went to the one who doesn't look.
So you looked, dear. That's a real difference between you and him.
And he doesn't look, dear, and the edge is right behind his heel.
But I won't rule on what your looking found, dear.
That's why looking early counts, dear, whatever it turns out to mean.
Let me look closer at what has been sitting just out of view…
